title: Fresh Lime Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Lime zest rubbed into the sugar and steeped in the custard, finished with fresh lime juice, instead of vanilla.
summary: Our classic French custard, made sharp and fragrant with lime: the zest is rubbed into the sugar and steeped in the hot custard, and fresh juice goes in just before chilling. Creamy but properly zingy.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make lime sugar
steps.text: Rub about three quarters of the lime zest into the sugar with your fingertips until it smells strongly of lime and feels slightly damp. Cover the remaining zest so it does not dry out.

steps.title: Warm the dairy
steps.text: Put the cream, milk, lime sugar and salt in the saucepan and stir over medium heat until the sugar has dissolved and the dairy is steaming.

steps.title: Temper the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks in the heatproof bowl, slowly whisk in about a third of the hot dairy, then pour everything back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Keep stirring over a low flame until the probe reads 77-80 °C and the custard clings to the spatula.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and leave for 30 min so the zest can perfume the custard.

steps.title: Add the juice
steps.text: Stir in the lime juice and the reserved zest, then strain into a bowl set in the iced water. Once cool, chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick, then pack into the container and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Zest the limes before juicing them; it is far easier.
A common mistake is adding the juice to the hot custard, which can make it grainy. Wait until it is off the heat and steeped.
Use only the green zest; the white pith underneath tastes bitter.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
